sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hi, Jason.
How you doing?
Oh, I was gonna say, what are the odds we got this right the first time, but it looks like.
Okay, let's just do this then.
Okay.
Sorry, we're in a meeting room and I just want to try to get this, this text sorted out, but it's like we're all set.
So thanks for making the time here with myself.
This is Alena, this is Matt.
Hello.
Hey, how you doing?
Good.
So sorry, what was the, what was the names again?
It's Matt and Alina.
Was it?
Yeah, you got it.
Perfect.
Full house.
How's it going?
Whereabouts you guys based?
Is it New York?
I'm normally on, on Vancouver island in, in Canada and they're both close to Toronto, but I'm, I'm in Toronto to today and tomorrow.
So you have the rare privilege of all three of us in the same room.
I was just looking at your yellow taxis and made a really bad judgment call, so.
Oh, forgive me.
Wow.
Okay.
So whereabouts are you?
I'm in London.
You're in London.
Okay then if you off, we're in the Midnight Oil.
The 7:30, 7:30pm Oil over here was.
4:30 at the moment.
Oh, of course.
I'm in, I'm, I'm in Ontario.
I'm used to the, I'm used to the eight hour difference.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, of course, of course.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
So yeah, not as big a difference as usual, I guess.
Yeah, yeah, exactly.
The west coast.
Yeah.
Well, great to meet you all and thank you for getting in touch.
So I'll start with a little bit about us and what we do and then it'd be great to hear about you guys and so we can see how we can help you.
So we're capital a group.
I believe you came via Agencies Co, which is our, our platform for sellers.
But we work on the buy and the sell side.

So we either work with buyers that are looking to acquire other agencies, if they're marketing agencies themselves, or we work with investment teams and private equity as well, helping them to build groups, agency groups.
And yeah, the agency's CO platform is for the sellers that we represent as well.
So the nice thing is working on the buy and sell sides, we know what a good deal looks like for our sellers, but also we know what, you know, offers are looking like as well for our buy side clients.
So be good to hear a little bit about you guys and what the plan is with Streetwise and then hopefully how we can help you to achieve your goals.
So there's There's a couple of agencies at play that we're looking at potentially merging here.
And, and then from there we would like to do a roll up.
We have a bunch of experience coming out of a roll up, a few of us, and so we've sort of seen what, what works, what doesn't work and feel fairly confident that we can, we can make a roll up work.
So just looking to apply that experience forward for ourselves over the next three to five years here.
Anything else we should add there?
That's fair.
Do you want us to describe a little bit more about these agencies or is that helpful?
Well, let's, let's find out a little bit more about your own agency or where you're at right now.
And then, yeah, let's get into the agencies you're looking to merge with.
That'd be helpful.
Yeah.
So the two of us, we both have an agency, Matt and I, Alina and I, and then Matt and a partner as well who's on our way here.
We both have agencies largely in the B2B space and pretty much run the gamut in terms of services.
I would say within digital marketing.
The only thing we don't do is pr.
Is there anything else we're missing in terms of capabilities?
I don't think so.
Yeah, so full service.
Everything from enterprise to small business in terms of customer profile.
So.
So the, the agency that all three of you own is Streetwise.
I know.
So Matt and Toby own Streetwise.
I have an agency with Alina called Found.
We are Found Ca.
I think I might have even started to book a call with Capital A through my Found email maybe.
And then this recognized the name.
So I'm sure I made it difficult for you and I apologize.
Okay, so there's two agencies and you guys represent the two agencies and you're looking to merge the company into, into.
A group or, you know, form a Holdco and have that buy the two or you know, whatever the most intelligent solution is there.
Okay.
All right.
And so what is, what is the.
So you just told me about we are Found then by saying that you, you do you run the Gamut?
No, that's both.
That would be the merged entity I described to you.
Yeah.
All right.
And then how far down the road are you with that merger?
Has it happened yet?
No, we would be.
So what we're doing is being cautious that the way in which we merge should also be speaking forward into the platform entity for the roll up.
Right.
So we're looking to avoid doing a bunch of legal work and then just having to unwind and redo that for purposes of a roll up.
So we're sort of, you know, considering, considering that in all this in terms of time and actions that we're taking.
Okay, so have you agreed how the roll up is work, is going to work between the two companies or in.
Terms of what exactly?
Equity, distribution, who owns what, who's in.
Charge, those types of things?
Yeah, we're, that's, that's why we're here for a couple days together.
Yeah, we figured it'd be good timing to talk to you and a couple other folks while we were together, you know.
Okay, cool.
All right, so.
So how can I, I help you?
So we're in a M and A advisory, so we, we generally work sort of end to end on deals.
So that includes sort of the, the bit that you've done already for yourselves and then helping to negotiate, you know, deals, valuations, etc.
And working on due diligence, etc.
Etc.
So we wouldn't normally come in at this later stage.
You normally work across the whole process.
So just kind of interested in what it is exactly that you are looking for help with.
So I mean you're saying about how to structure the business and things like that.
Is that what you're looking for?

I think broadly the next sort of 8 to 12 acquisitions is where you guys would come up again in the roll up here and then of interest, I'm on your email list now and so I'm seeing things about how either agencies or Capital A is doing their own roll up or something like that.
So I'm not sure exactly.
We're in the process of putting together a roll up.
So we've probably got about five or six agencies that we're speaking to at the moment and merging them together.
So we're looking for agencies that are doing around 1 million in EBITDA or more.
And we're looking for five to eight agencies around that size to roll up together, then exit to private equity.
So that's what we're looking to do.
So I'm happy to give you more information about that.
But obviously you guys are in the throes of doing this merger yourself and it sounds like once you've done that you're going to make a number of acquisitions as well.
I think just, just from what your question is at the moment, it seems to be possibly a legal question which I can't answer.
Or maybe your accountant in terms of like how you would structure the business.
I can some sort of general Overview but really it's probably stuff that you know already.
So the cleanest way for you guys to do it going forward is probably to create a hold code and then work out who is it worth what.
And then you would split the equity and the ownership across all of the shareholders and put that into the hold code.
And then in terms of making more acquisitions going forward, there's a few different ways that you could do it.
So a lot of, a lot of acquisition companies, vehicles like to do it really clean where they just take the assets out of the business.
So what you can do is actually you can give equity to the, the companies through their own business that they own today.
And then the, the, the, the assets go into the holdco and then you just create a new service business for each.
If you're going to keep the company, you create a new service business that's owned 100% by the whole co.
And then the shareholdings just diluted.
For the founders that come in.
Obviously if you're paying them cash then the amount that they get that you would get diluted would be less and less depend on, on how that's structured.
So but, but that probably is something for your accountant at the point where, where that happens.
But initially I guess you're at the point now where you need to decide structure and whether you're going to set the old code company up.
Yeah, so that's the goal of the next sort of 48 hours.
Not that we started this morning but you know, just kind of finalizing that.
Right.
And then like I say, we've done, done quite a bit of this in the last five years.

Probably something like 13 transactions, lots of integrations, you know, you name it in terms of asset purchases and you know, founders keeping minority shares in the their entity, full shares to the parent entity, all that kind of stuff.
And so you guys would come in once we were merged.
I wonder.
Yeah, I mean that's what we're, we're experts in.
So we can really accelerate that process.
So to give you an example of how that normally works, so we would work with a group like yourselves, we would be able to go out to the market.
Basically we're looking for off market deals.
What you don't want to do is buy from brokers because if you're knocking on brokers doors, they're just going to give you businesses where founders are looking to get out most of the time.
Not always.
There are some good deals to be had there but everybody's knocking on the same doors.
So the sellers are really in the driver's seat.
We did a lot of that and I was actually the one who was sourcing the off market deal.
So I think we were saying maybe on market as an exception if we loved something.
But largely, yeah, it's okay to have.
It in the mix but you know, don't get your hands because you're against, you know, 10 other buyers.
So yeah, really the seller and the, the M and A team should be in the driving seat for that and pushing the price.
So you want to be outside of those pros, those types of processes as a buyer.
And that's how we help our clients.
So we help really compress time.
What would take you a couple of years to get a couple of businesses closed we can do in around six months.
So what we're doing is scaling up that outbound, those outbound conversations.
And we do that via some tools that we have in House on LinkedIn and through cold email.
But we've got a database of 130,000 marketing agencies already.
We're always speaking to founders as you know, if you're on our mailing list, that's basically keeping everybody warm.
So when we reach out, we tend to have a good reception as well, which is a different reception than most sort of agencies would have if they try to go and find agencies to buy.
Because other agency owners are very defensive.
They feel like people are fishing those types of things.
So we're able to scale up those conversations and have lots of them very quickly and figure out who is the tire kicker, who's actually in the market who would accept and offer those types of things.
And we can usually bring about three to five deals a week.
So we're having those initial screening calls.
We're making sure they're a good fit for what you want to do.
And then we have a weekly meeting with our clients and we set up the calls with the ones that you really like.
So that tends to take about two months of doing that if you, if you're not too busy with other stuff.
And then we'll get some offers on the table and hopefully close one or two of those, those deals down.
Like I say, it usually is about six month process to get at least one done.
But we've done two within six months as well.
So it really does depend on the team and whether you're open to getting offers out and getting deals closed.
But as you all know already, I mean it sounds like you guys have been busy, but it's a volume play.
You really need to be speaking to 10 agencies.
If you want to close one deal and you have to make lots of offers because a lot of them will fall over during negotiations.
You know, people pull out right at the 12th hour and you've just got no way of knowing who that's going to be.
It always feels really great at the start.
So it's about you.
I'm really just keeping as many of those conversations going until you've got the deals, the amount of deals closed as you have.
And it's always good to have a full pipeline and not close it.
So we're really helping with, and that's our expertise.
It would be good to get into that and help you guys once you've closed in 48 hours.
So what is it that you, you are looking for to add on to the, what are you going to be called by the way?
Street Found, Found Wise.
Found Wise?
Yeah, something like that.
Yeah.
You know, we'll, we'll start probably with, with things that match us Again.
A lot of what we'll do is based on what we saw over the last five years and that other roll up.
So we'll look at things that are complementary.
We won't get too core expertise.
So you know, the first couple will definitely be B2B.
They won't be too big.

You know, they'll probably be 2 million 1 to 3 in revenue, 300 to call it 800 in, in EBITDA in Canadian dollars and you know, culture fit, founder fit, no rule, all that good stuff is what we'll be looking for.
Yeah, okay, brilliant.
And so service wise, you don't know, I mean, be good for me to keep my eyes open over the next couple of weeks.
Well, you sent one this morning that was interesting, which was a PR because like I say, the, the one thing we don't have is, is PR as a competency.
So I think you had a million in revenue or a million in EBITDA, one of those things.
900,000 maybe in revenue.
PR One that I saw this morning.
Yeah, it's, it's based in Georgia.
That one, 700K American dollars.
Okay.
Yeah.
So, yeah, so, so you're in London but you're dealing.
Like what's, what's the, what's the location spread here?
Like are you dealing largely in US stuff?
Are you dealing in Europe and uk?
Like what's, what's it look like?
Yeah.
So our focus really is North America.
Most of our clients are in the us Even when we were on the, the, the hunt for European or UK based agencies, the buyers tend to be American.
They've just got a really strong economy, even though Trump's trying his best to, to mess it up.
But, but yeah, we tend to work in the U.S.
however, you know, we are representing sellers in Hong Kong.
We've done a deal in Israel which we sold to a US listed company.
And we, we've got stuff in Turkey and, and Paris.
I mean, we're, we're listing agencies across the, the globe, really.
So are you still working with Hubble Digital?
Because we know them quite well or one of our people know them quite well?
Well, we haven't done, we've done two deals with those guys, though.
We work with them directly on the buy side, so we, we source both of those deals.
Okay, cool.
That's good.
Yeah, but I haven't spoke to them for about a year now.
Super busy.
But yeah, I mean, by all means, check in with those guys to get a good reference.
Yeah.
What question for me would be, what are we missing?
So if we're working with you, what is missing from the equation?

Like, because we, we've had conversations with another group that's sort of proposing a, you can almost think of it as an outsourced approach to this whole thing, like sourcing, you know, sources of debt, finding, finding deals, potentially like the whole sort of gamut, even integration stuff.
But when we were talking about legal and accounting at the start of the call.
So what would we be missing or what would we have to bolt on in working with you, with you folks that wouldn't be part of that equation?
Yeah.
So we work start to finish as your M and A team.
But what we are not is we're not your legal team and we're not your financial advisors.
So if you were speaking to an investment bank, that's probably what they would be offering is the extra stuff that you've said.
And investment banks also have their own legal teams as well.
But that kind of keeps you locked into just one set of advice.
And you know, from my point of view, I don't always think that's necessarily the best way to go, although I don't.

I hate like when our clients have a completely different legal team that, that, you know, with a completely different view because often those, those are the most expensive ones and they tend to drag things out.
But I would certainly say you would probably need your own legal advice separate to whoever you're working with on the M and A side of things.
But we don't supply any of that.
What we are really good at is going out and sort of Talking, we're like agency owner whisperers.
We are great at going out, finding companies that are really good fit, and then easing them into a relationship with our clients.
You know, quite often there's huge amounts of emotional responses that, that come out of agency owners.
I mean, they're creative people, they don't tend to want to work with people.
They don't understand the M and A process.

And that's what we're really good at is, you know, easing them into the conversations and guiding them and being a cushion and actually being a sounding board for both sides as well and getting those deals done.
So that's where our expertise lies.
If you're talking to investment bankers, then I see them partly as the problem to M and A for marketing agencies because they speak in a different language, they're often rude and weird and.
Well, I'm not saying agency owners aren't rude and weird, but investment banks have their own way of working which I think rubs up against the agency founders themselves.
So that's what we are, we're a bridge between them and us, I would say.
Yeah.
And what do you make of the fact that you, you guys are going through this roll up project on your own?
Do you see that as in any way weird or like creating a competitive dynamic if we're doing the same thing?
Or could these things be, be, I don't know, helpful to each other in some way?
So we are constantly reaching out to agencies in different places, both on the buy and the sell side.
Everybody's got their own unique set of preferences for what they're looking to create.
You know, yours may be geographic.

For instance, you look, you're looking for stuff in Canada, whereas other clients are looking for really specific verticals that they're working in might be legal or veterinarian or, you know, we have all sorts of different client requests and very rarely do we can we sort of bump up against two different clients.
And I think the same thing is, is applicable to what we're trying to achieve.
We're actually looking for roll ups in very narrow verticals ourselves.
And these companies are 1 million plus in EBITDA.
And I would say a lot of our clients don't even buy companies that are that big.
They tend to buy smaller.
There's a sweet spot of revenue between 1 and 5 million.
And most of our clients actually look to buy those smaller agencies and not agencies that are slightly above that.
And that's what we're looking to roll up.
Our aim is to create a company that is around 5 to 8 million in EBITDA.
And those companies are really attractive for private equity.

So we are creating those platforms and we are handing back the multiples that normally private equity would take from an agency owner by buying them at 5x and then selling them to another private equity company, 8x and pocketing the difference.

What we're doing is giving that difference back to agency owners and putting together five businesses to make a PL, to make one platform business and sell them once at 8 or 10x and give that, that, that margin back to the founders of those businesses.
So I would hope that in, you know, 90% of the cases that's not going to rub up against any of our clients and where it is, we will just be really transparent.
You know, if we've had a conversation with somebody and hasn't worked out, then we can, we can hand that over to our clients if they're looking for something similar and vice versa.
So is that something you intended to keep doing?
I mean, I know you're doing one right now.
If that has a time horizon of what, a year or two and then you'll do another one or what does that look like?
Yeah, so we're, like I said, we're in a couple of different verticals with that.
You know, what we want to do is stack around particular services or particular buyers.
So for instance, we don't want to put B2B and B2C agencies in the same mix, but these agencies can work in separate verticals.
So it's likely that we will focus just on the first one for about 12 months.
But if we get enough candidates in another one, then we can start building a second or third of these types of roll ups.
We actually work with investment bankers, I guess you would call them, who do these types of roll ups all the time and they come to us to sell them.
So we actually work on the sell side, helping other roll ups exit without taking as much of the upside.
So just the only difference in this occasion is that we will take some of that upside ourselves rather than taking percentage of somebody else's.
But yeah, I mean it's a recyclable thing.
We've built the agencies agency a platform to do exactly this as a white label platform where we can constantly build and sell into private equity or larger agency holding companies.
What about how do you structure your fees?
So on the buy side we work on a retained basis, so it's 5,000 US a month and then we take one and a half percent on the close.
So whatever the full valuation of the business is we usually take 50% of that on the close and then three year earn out.
We take our fee every time the cash is released to the seller of.
The overall value of the combined entry.
Yes.
So basically what?
Yeah, yeah.
If our client buys something for 10 million, for instance, it's 5 million up front.
We take 100 on the cash up front and then every, every year when they pay the client, the seller again, we take one and a half percent on that as a fee.
Perfect.
Yeah, I can send all that in a, in an email after, so you can see.
Yeah, that'd be great.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
It's pretty straightforward.
I mean we've just done a couple of deals for one company called Skyview and we're still in the roll up process with these guys.
So we've done two deals already.
We have another two in the pipeline that we're probably going to close over the next couple of weeks that are quite small and then we have some larger ones as bolt ons as well.
So they bought a company called Hovercraft in the US that's based.
Where is it based?
In the north Northwest somewhere.
Denver.
And then we bought a company called OMM in the UK and now we're buying a few more US businesses to roll in and a UK one as well in fact.
So, so yeah, and they were just an investment group that was two guys, they'd retired from cloud computing and they'd done a few roll ups themselves.
Bit like you guys, it sounds like.
And they just wanted to do one more before they retired to the golf course full time.
So one more job.
Yeah, so they were, they were a good example of how we can really create value for them.
Because it was quite difficult on their own.
They were approaching agencies and the agency owners were saying like, well who are you guys?
You're nothing to do with the agency.
Well, you don't understand what we're doing.
So we kind of got them from 0 to 20 million in a very short space of time.
Took about eight months I think, to do both those acquisitions.
So.
It sounds like our current size isn't a limitation for you.
Like you're not, you're not, you don't have a sort of minimum size that you're willing to work with.
I mean it's different for us because we're kind of on a building pathway here.
But you're not, you're not averse to us at our current size.
Not at all, no.
I've just got another call at 5:00 on my time.
Not at all.
We, we are.
My preference is to work with founders like yourselves.

You know what I don't enjoy is working with big corporates and we do sell into corporates but we tend to stop dealing with the founders once they have their corp dev teams and they tend to be sort of younger investment banker guys.
I've got no idea about the creative process and anything else so it becomes a bit of a yawn fest with these.
So I would much rather work with founders like yourselves that are ambitious and just looking to, to build something and that's where I can really add value.
So yeah, 100% I'm happy to work with you guys.
Well, we'll let you get to another to your other call but thanks very much.
Yeah, thanks Andy.
This was super helpful.
Yeah, no problem.
So I'll stick the the terms, you know, for a buy side in an email, put some in the diary for maybe like two weeks and I'll chase you up and see where you guys got to with with your official.
Yeah.
So yeah, congratulations on finding each other and cheers on getting the deal.

summary.action_items:
**Andy Day**
Send email with buy-side terms and fee structure details to Jason (29:47)
Schedule follow-up call in approximately two weeks to check on merger progress (29:47)

**Jason Smith**
Finalize merger structure with team within 48 hours (12:40)
Review Capital A's fee structure and services once received (27:09)
Determine equity distribution and leadership structure for the merged entity (07:57)
summary.overview: In the recent Business Development and M&A Strategy Meeting, participants Jason Smith and Andy Day discussed the merger of two B2B digital marketing agencies—Streetwise and Found—as a precursor to a larger roll-up strategy. The meeting focused on the careful consideration of merger structure, equity distribution, and leadership roles to align with future growth plans. Andy Day presented Capital A Group's M&A advisory services, emphasizing their approach to streamline acquisition timelines by leveraging a database of potential off-market agencies, and provided insights on fee structures involved in their collaboration. Both teams identified initial acquisition targets, prioritizing agencies with revenues between $1-3 million and EBITDA of $300-800K CAD, and noted the potential for integrating PR agencies into their service offerings. Action items included follow-ups on merger progress and financial arrangements, demonstrating a proactive approach to their strategic goals.
summary.short_summary: In the recent Business Development and M&A Strategy Meeting, Jason Smith and Andy Day discussed the merger of Streetwise and Found, two B2B digital marketing agencies, setting the stage for a larger roll-up strategy. They emphasized the importance of carefully structuring the merger to ensure alignment with future growth plans, considering equity distribution and leadership roles. Andy presented the services of Capital A Group, highlighting their M&A advisory approach that leverages a database of 130,000 agencies to streamline acquisition timelines. Both teams identified initial acquisition targets, focusing on agencies with revenues between $1-3 million and EBITDA of $300-800K CAD, and expressed interest in integrating PR agencies into their offerings. Action items included follow-ups on merger progress and financial arrangements, reflecting a proactive attitude towards achieving their strategic objectives.
